newsitem.title: UK: UK's gas hard landing trouble-free in early stages.
newsitem.headline: UK's gas hard landing trouble-free in early stages.

text.p: Daily balancing on the UK's spot natural gas market is working so smoothly that operator TransCo -- the pipeline arm of British Gas Plc -- has only had to balance once in the first 10 days of the month.
"Before the hard landing came in (on September 1), we were balancing three or four times a week," said TransCo spokesman Mike Walpole. "Since then, we've only had to do it once".

Under the "hard landing" -- or Phase II of the Network Code which regulates use of TransCo's pipeline network, the National Transmission System (NTS) -- shippers using the system are required to balance daily.

This means they have to ensure that inputs of gas into the NTS match offtakes, or deliveries to customers. Failure to do so results in a financial penalty on a sliding scale, with larger imbalances incurring bigger penalties.

TransCo operates a new market instrument -- the flexibility mechanism -- which allows shippers to balance at short notice by bidding to buy or sell using a screen-based system with TransCo the only counterparty. This has also been very quiet recently.

Walpole said there was no activity on the flexibility market at all during September 1-9 except for September 5 when there were three "system outputs", or movements of gas out of the NTS, and nine "system inputs". All prices were between 12.20 and 12.60 pence a therm, slightly below spot prices at the time.
"There's evidence that a dozen or so shippers are now operating a 24-hour cover arrangement (to use the flexibility mechanism)," Walpole said. "This has not happened on that sort of scale before.
"As far as daily balancing is concerned, shippers are doing it all themselves."

Traders agree that the early stages of the hard landing have gone smoothly. "People were well prepared for the hard landing and have flexibility already," said one. "So far there hasn't been much scurrying around looking for gas for the day ahead."

Britain's natural gas market has been deregulated in stages since the initial privatisation of former monopoly British Gas in 1986. Deregulation should be completed by 1998 when householders across the country will be able to buy gas from any licensed supplier.
